question: How did ancient civilizations view the primary cause of illness?
explanation: Early societies largely believed that sickness came from angry gods or evil spirits rather than physical germs. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which ancient society is best known for building early military hospitals?
explanation: Roman rulers established dedicated medical stations to treat injured soldiers and maintain a strong fighting force. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which institution drove most healthcare delivery during the Middle Ages?
explanation: Monasteries and religious orders took primary responsibility for sheltering and nursing the sick during this era. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: What motivated individuals to join nursing orders during the medieval period?
explanation: Caregiving was seen as a holy duty rather than a secular profession pursued for money. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: What was the main factor that reduced soldier deaths in Crimea under Nightingale?
explanation: Nightingale focused heavily on environmental hygiene, fresh air, and clean water to stop the spread of infection. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is the opening of the Nightingale Training School considered a major milestone?

options.A: It replaced doctors as heads of hospitals
options.B: It guaranteed high government salaries for all graduates
options.C: It allowed nurses to perform independent surgeries
options.D: It separated nursing education from domestic servitude

explanation: Establishing a formal school ensured nurses were trained systematically rather than just learning on the job without guidance. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Who introduced Western-style nursing and hospitals to Nigeria?
explanation: Western healthcare structures were brought over during the colonial era alongside missionary religious expansion. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: What was a major effect of establishing the Nursing Council for Nigeria in 1930?

options.A: Placing nurses in charge of military bases
options.C: Removing foreign nurses from the country

explanation: The council provided official oversight to ensure practitioners met specific educational and ethical standards. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of professional nursing regulatory bodies?

options.A: To negotiate high salaries with hospital owners
options.B: To provide funding for private clinics
options.C: To conduct political lobbying for governments
options.D: To protect the public through quality standards

explanation: Boards and councils ensure that only qualified, ethical individuals are permitted to care for patients. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: How has nursing education changed from its early hospital apprenticeship days?

options.A: It moved into higher institutions with a research focus
options.B: It shortened training to less than one month
options.C: It became entirely focused on home remedies
options.D: It removed all clinical bedside practice requirements

explanation: Modern nursing programs award degrees and emphasize evidence-based practice grounded in scientific research. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which tool has largely replaced paper charting in modern healthcare facilities?
explanation: Digital systems store patient data securely and allow fast sharing among healthcare team members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: A nurse uses a computer video link to assess a patient living in a remote rural village. What trend does this represent?
explanation: Telemedicine uses telecommunications technology to deliver healthcare services across geographical distances. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)
